rv.q: It is one of the best plays you’ll ever see.
This dodgy charmer is a glorious creation.
You could watch this play, and Rylance’s performance, every night of the too-short run and still find new dimensions to wonder at.
One reason Jerusalem was and remains so remarkable is that it is so different from the boring compliance of most other new drama.
Together, this exemplary ensemble give us a breath-taking portrait of backwater England that roves from the profane to the sublime, a crucial theatrical rite, fit for the ages.
For a few months, it has returned to our dark, satanic mills.
For all its interplay of past and present, reality and myth, it's a phenomenal piece of theatre.
With Rylance in the role, its spell is irresistible.
Rylance’s Rooster is surely the greatest performance of the century.
Butterworth’s infinitely rich play is proof that legends age well.
It is quite simply just wondrous.
In a thrilling revival that opened Thursday at the Apollo Theater (running through Aug. 7), everything feels enriched by time.
Wild and whimsical, uproarious and desolate, Butterworth’s play is still a mighty force of irrepressible live theatre.

This brilliant, highly topical three-hour twenty-minute play, that seems to pass very quickly, takes us through his nine-hour day with the outcasts and the escapees from the dull life of the world beyond the forest.
It is a staggering and immersive experience that exhilarates to watch and elevates both those on stage and the spellbound audience.
What I do know is that this is a massive, durable, relevant and joyful work that is served superbly here by a flawless cast.
Mark Rylance proves he is leading actor of a generation.

cn.t: Rylance delivers a career-defining performance in this triumphant revival of Butterworth's modern masterpiece about myth and Englishness. Critics hail the production's enduring power and relevance, though a few question the play's mythologized status.

vr.q: I give Jerusalem five stars but it's actually in a class of its own; if you haven't seen it do everything you can to get a ticket.
